Availability Date Defaults.what: Sets the default before-start and after-end availability behavior for new assignments and discussions.
steps: For an early-access ticket, distinguish hiding an activity from showing its title while restricting access or submissions.
Availability Date Defaults sets the starting choices for new assignments and discussions; adjust the existing activity itself when fixing a current ticket.
Check both its start/end dates and the behavior attached to each date; a date alone does not explain what learners can see.
Availability Date Defaults.result: New activities use the selected defaults; an existing activity still needs its own dates and availability checked.
Availability Date Defaults.ticket: “I want students to see the assignment title before they can submit.”
Availability Date Defaults.scope: Real-screen steps are documented; this destination was not captured and is not interactive in this lab. The linked institutional guide documents this exact entry; available choices depend on the tool.

Course Offering Information.what: Holds course-level details such as the course name, active status, and access dates.
steps: Course is active and the course start/end dates control course-level access; these are separate from an assignment or quiz’s dates.
For an enrolled learner who cannot open the course, check those settings in Course Offering Information, then confirm their enrollment and role.
Save the intended course settings and verify access for the affected role; instructor access does not establish learner access.
Course Offering Information.result: An enrolled learner can access the course when its status, dates, and role permissions allow it.
Course Offering Information.ticket: “My students are enrolled but cannot open the course.”
Course Offering Information.scope: The real destination was not captured; this lab offers a simplified practice form for course details, status, and dates.

Homepages.what: Chooses the page learners reach when they open Course Home and the layout used there.
steps: Identify the active homepage and whether it is widget-based, a tool page, or an external URL; that determines what Course Home displays.
For a missing Announcements panel, edit the active widget-based homepage and check whether that widget is present.
To replace the landing page, select the approved choice under Active Homepage and Apply; an enforced institutional homepage may prevent this.
Homepages.result: Course Home displays the selected homepage; an institution-enforced homepage may prevent changing it.
Homepages.ticket: “The course home page is missing our usual announcements panel.”
Homepages.scope: Real-screen steps are documented; this destination was not captured and is not interactive in this lab.

Navigation & Themes.what: Controls the course navigation links and their visual theme.
steps: A navbar controls the links learners see; a theme controls its appearance, while tool availability is managed separately.
For a missing Discussions link, edit an editable navbar and use Add Links, or create a course navbar when the inherited one cannot be edited.
Select the saved navbar under Active Navbar and Apply, then check access with the intended role.
Navigation & Themes.result: The selected navbar exposes the chosen links; removing a link does not disable its tool.
Navigation & Themes.ticket: “How do I put Discussions on the course navigation bar?”
Navigation & Themes.scope: Real-screen steps are documented; this destination was not captured and is not interactive in this lab.

Widgets.what: Creates and manages the content blocks that can appear on a widget-based homepage.
steps: A widget is one block within a homepage, such as a welcome message; changing a widget and choosing the active homepage are different tasks.
Use Create Widget for a custom welcome panel, configure its name and content, then add it to the active widget-based homepage.
If the panel is missing, check the active homepage, widget placement, and any restrictions before recreating it.
Widgets.result: The widget appears after it is added to the active homepage, not merely after it is created.
Widgets.ticket: “I need a welcome message box on my course home page.”
Widgets.scope: Real-screen steps are documented; this destination was not captured and is not interactive in this lab.

Calendar.what: Shows course events and dates so learners can see what is coming up.
steps: Create Event is appropriate for an office-hour session or class event; an assessment’s deadline should be maintained in the assessment.
For an event, set its title, When, and any recurrence or group restrictions, then Create.
For a wrong assessment date on the calendar, inspect the linked assessment’s dates before adding a second calendar entry.
Calendar.result: The new event appears on the calendar; assessment deadlines should still be checked in the assessment itself.
Calendar.ticket: “How can I add next week’s office hours to the course calendar?”
Calendar.scope: Real-screen steps are documented; this destination was not captured and is not interactive in this lab.

Content.what: Organizes course learning materials and activity links into modules and topics.
steps: In Classic Content, modules organize topics; a file in Manage Files needs a Content topic or another learner-facing link to be findable.
For a reading, use the module’s Upload/Create > Upload Files; use Existing Activities when linking an assignment or quiz that already exists.
For missing material, inspect the topic and parent module’s visibility, dates, and release conditions, then test the actual linked resource.
Content.result: Learners can find the material in Content when its visibility, dates, and release conditions permit access.
Content.ticket: “I uploaded the reading, but students cannot find it in the course.”
Content.scope: The capture shows Classic Content with a New Content Experience prompt; this lab models a limited Content workflow, and other experiences have different controls.

Course Builder.what: Provides a visual course outline where you can arrange modules, learning objects, and placeholders.
steps: Use the visual outline to arrange modules and learning objects; placeholders let you plan work before the actual resource exists.
For a weekly outline, add the modules and placeholders, then replace each placeholder with the required content or activity.
Review the resulting Content structure and activity settings; an organized outline does not finish assessment configuration.
Course Builder.result: The course structure is organized, but a placeholder still needs content before it becomes usable learning material.
Course Builder.ticket: “I want to plan the weekly course structure before adding all the readings.”
Course Builder.scope: Real-screen steps are documented; this destination was not captured and is not interactive in this lab.

Course Design Accelerator.what: Offers a course-design entry point for supported course-building tasks when enabled by the institution.
steps: Use this course-design entry point only for the workflows your institution enables; official documentation confirms its role-based availability.
For a new-course request, inspect the available design choices and continue in the linked setup tools; exact current controls require your local screen.
Course Design Accelerator.result: You reach the supported design workflow; the exact options must be checked on your institution’s screen.
Course Design Accelerator.ticket: “I see Course Design Accelerator but do not know whether to use it to start my course.”
Course Design Accelerator.scope: This destination was not captured and is not interactive here; official permissions documentation confirms the tool, but its exact current screen sequence is not verified.

External Learning Tools.what: Connects a course to external learning services through Learning Tools Interoperability, often called LTI.
steps: Separate a launch failure from a grade-return failure: they may involve different provider settings even when they affect the same activity.
Identify the provider, course link, and approved deployment; confirm that the deployment is shared to this course.
Check the failing stage with the institution’s integration administrator; course links cannot repair missing organization-level registration or provider credentials.
External Learning Tools.result: The support ticket identifies the correct link or deployment to repair without guessing at provider credentials.
External Learning Tools.ticket: “The publisher homework link opens an error instead of the activity.”
External Learning Tools.scope: Real-screen steps are documented; this destination was not captured and is not interactive in this lab. Provider registration, deployment, external launches, and grade return require the real institution and provider services.

Forms.what: Creates ePortfolio form templates that learners complete as structured reflection or evidence artifacts.
steps: These are ePortfolio form templates: the learner’s completed response becomes an artifact, such as a placement reflection.
Create or adjust the template fields, then make the template available through Content and specify how the resulting artifact should be shared or submitted.
If you need anonymous course feedback rather than an ePortfolio artifact, use Surveys instead.
Forms.result: Learners create their own completed ePortfolio form artifacts from the template.
Forms.ticket: “I need a structured reflection form that students can keep in their ePortfolio.”
Forms.scope: Real-screen steps are documented; this destination was not captured and is not interactive in this lab.

Frequently Asked Questions.what: Publishes reusable answers to common course questions, organized into categories.
steps: Categories organize reusable answers, such as submission rules or course logistics; questions must be placed in the appropriate category.
Use New Category if needed, then New Question to enter the question and answer; verify that learners can reach FAQ.
Frequently Asked Questions.result: The saved answer is available in its category to learners who can access FAQ.
Frequently Asked Questions.ticket: “Where can I put answers to questions students ask every week?”
Frequently Asked Questions.scope: Real-screen steps are documented; this destination was not captured and is not interactive in this lab.

Glossary.what: Provides a course dictionary of important terms and definitions.
steps: Use New Term for a course-specific definition and optionally connect it to a relevant Content topic.
For a terminology request, maintain the authoritative definition here and check that learners have a route to the glossary.
Glossary.result: Learners can look up the saved definition in the course glossary.
Glossary.ticket: “How do I give students one place to look up the course terminology?”
Glossary.scope: Real-screen steps are documented; this destination was not captured and is not interactive in this lab.

Import / Export / Copy Components.what: Moves supported course materials into or out of a course, including copying from another course offering.
steps: Start in the destination course; Copy Components from another Org Unit brings material from an accessible source course into this one.
Select the source and components deliberately: repeating a copy can create duplicates, and linked activities may need their associated components.
After copying, review dates, visibility, external links, and assessment associations before releasing the course.
Import / Export / Copy Components.result: Selected components appear in the destination; repeated copies can create duplicates and copied dates need review.
Import / Export / Copy Components.ticket: “I need last term’s content and assessments in my new course shell.”
Import / Export / Copy Components.scope: Real-screen steps are documented; this destination was not captured and is not interactive in this lab.

Instructional Design Wizard.what: Helps plan a course blueprint that can be developed further in Course Builder.
steps: Treat the wizard as course planning: its blueprint can be developed in Course Builder.
Review the proposed modules and activities, then populate their placeholders and configure the actual assessments; the exact wizard sequence requires the local screen.
Instructional Design Wizard.result: The plan supplies a course structure that still needs completed learning materials and assessment settings.
Instructional Design Wizard.ticket: “I have learning goals but need help turning them into a course outline.”
Instructional Design Wizard.scope: The official Course Builder guide describes this relationship; the wizard’s exact screens were not captured and are not interactive here.

Learning Activity Library.what: Provides teaching-activity ideas and descriptions to support course planning.
steps: Use the library to select a teaching approach that fits a learning goal, such as reflection, discussion, or application.
Translate the idea into an actual activity in Content, Discussions, or Assignments; this is a planning resource, distinct from the Learning Repository’s reusable objects.
Learning Activity Library.result: You have an activity design to implement; browsing this library does not by itself assign work to learners.
Learning Activity Library.ticket: “I need ideas for an activity that helps students apply this week’s concepts.”
Learning Activity Library.scope: This legacy destination was not captured and is not interactive here; the linked D2L Community discussion supplies context, not a verified current click-by-click guide.

Links.what: Organizes useful course web links into categories.
steps: Categories organize reusable web resources, such as library guides; a link title should explain the destination to learners.
Use New Link with the appropriate category, title, and URL, then test the destination and any sign-in requirement.
Links.result: The link is available in its category; learners still need access to any external site it opens.
Links.ticket: “Where should I collect the websites my students need for this course?”
Links.scope: Real-screen steps are documented; this destination was not captured and is not interactive in this lab.

Manage Dates.what: Reviews and updates dates across supported course items from one place.
steps: Bulk Edit Dates assigns specific new dates; Bulk Offset Dates shifts existing dates forward or backward by a chosen number of days.
After a course copy, select only the intended items and date types so you do not unintentionally shift exceptions or unrelated events.
Inspect representative activities afterward, including the difference between due dates and dates that restrict access.
Manage Dates.result: The selected supported dates change together, reducing the work needed after copying a course.
Manage Dates.ticket: “All of last term’s due dates copied over; how can I move them?”
Manage Dates.scope: An empty Manage Dates screen was captured; selecting items and bulk date changes were not observed and are not interactive here.

Manage Files.what: Stores and organizes the files used by the course’s pages and learning materials.
steps: This is the course’s file storage; Content supplies the learner-facing structure and links to those files.
For a broken reading, confirm that the expected file exists and that the Content topic points to the correct path.
Upload or repair the intended resource, then test the topic; renaming, moving, or deleting files can break existing links.
Manage Files.result: The file is stored in the course and has a working learner-facing link when you add it to Content.
Manage Files.ticket: “My reading file exists in the course, but there is no link for students to open it.”
Manage Files.scope: Real-screen steps are documented; this destination was not captured and is not interactive in this lab.

Attendance.what: Records attendance for named course sessions using a register and an attendance-status scheme.
steps: A register groups the sessions you track; its attendance scheme defines statuses and their percentage values.
For weekly labs, create a register and sessions, then record each learner’s status per session.
If a percentage looks wrong, check the scheme: a status with no assigned percentage is treated differently from an absence worth zero.
Attendance.result: The register shows session attendance and calculates attendance percentages from the chosen scheme.
Attendance.ticket: “How can I record who attended each weekly lab?”
Attendance.scope: Real-screen steps are documented; this destination was not captured and is not interactive in this lab.

Class Progress.what: Shows learner activity and progress indicators that help you investigate participation questions.
steps: Start with the named learner and the relevant indicator, such as Content, Assignments, or Quizzes, instead of assuming low activity means missing work.
Compare progress indicators with the underlying submission or attempt; access data is evidence of activity, not proof of comprehension.
Use the result to narrow the ticket to visibility, participation, submission, or evaluation.
Class Progress.result: You have activity evidence to guide support, while recognizing that an access record alone does not prove understanding.
Class Progress.ticket: “Can I check whether a student opened the reading or submitted the assignment?”
Class Progress.scope: Real-screen steps are documented; this destination was not captured and is not interactive in this lab.

Classlist.what: Lists course participants and provides permitted participant-management and accommodation actions.
steps: Edit Accommodations applies to a learner across course quizzes; quiz Special Access is for an exception on a particular quiz.
Under Modify Time Limit, Multiplier of original quiz time scales every affected quiz, while Extra time adds a fixed number of minutes.
For a 1.5-times accommodation, enter that multiplier and save; inspect any quiz-specific Special Access before predicting the learner’s final time.
Classlist.result: The course accommodation supplies the learner’s quiz-time adjustment; inspect quiz-specific Special Access for any separate override.
Classlist.ticket: “This student needs one and a half times the usual time on all course quizzes.”
Classlist.scope: The Classlist and accommodation controls were captured; saving accommodations and the resulting timing are simplified practice behavior here.

Groups.what: Organizes learners into course groups for collaboration, restricted activities, or group submissions.
steps: A category defines a set of groups; Enrollment Type determines whether membership is assigned, automatic, or chosen through self-enrollment.
For project teams, configure the group count or size, then verify actual membership before connecting group assignments or discussions.
If a learner cannot see team work, check both their group membership and the activity’s group/category restrictions.
Groups.result: Learners belong to the intended course groups, which can then be used by supported activities.
Groups.ticket: “I need teams of four for the group project.”
Groups.scope: Real-screen steps are documented; this destination was not captured and is not interactive in this lab.

Assignments.what: Collects learner work and provides submission, evaluation, feedback, and grade settings.
steps: The due date marks the deadline; start/end dates and their availability behavior determine when learners can view or submit.
For one learner’s extension, use the assignment’s Special Access and select that learner instead of moving the whole class’s deadline.
Check the exception’s due/access dates, assignment visibility, submission type, and grade association, then save the intended settings.
Assignments.result: Learners can submit under the configured rules; a due date and an availability end date have different effects.
Assignments.ticket: “One student needs extra time to submit this assignment.”
Assignments.scope: Assignment creation and Special Access controls were captured; submission, evaluation, and saved Special Access outcomes were not observed, and the lab models only selected settings.

Awards.what: Recognizes learner achievements with badges or certificates issued manually or through conditions.
steps: Awards may be issued manually or automatically through release conditions; determine which process the badge or certificate uses.
For a missing badge, inspect its exact criteria and the learner’s recorded completion or score, not just their claim to have finished.
Check the learner’s award record and any issuing conditions before manually issuing a duplicate.
Awards.result: Eligible learners receive the selected award when the configured issuing process completes.
Awards.ticket: “A student finished orientation but did not receive the completion badge.”
Awards.scope: Real-screen steps are documented; this destination was not captured and is not interactive in this lab.

Checklists.what: Gives learners a list of course tasks they can mark complete themselves.
steps: Checklists are learner-maintained task lists; checking an item is different from submitting an assignment or earning a grade.
Create the checklist and a category, then add tasks such as reading a chapter or preparing for a lab, with dates or links where useful.
Place the checklist in Content so it sits alongside the week’s actual learning activities.
Checklists.result: Learners can track their own completion; a checked box is not a graded assessment result.
Checklists.ticket: “Can I give students a tick-off list of everything they should do each week?”
Checklists.scope: Real-screen steps are documented; this destination was not captured and is not interactive in this lab.

Competencies.what: Tracks achievement through a structure of competencies, learning objectives, and associated activities.
steps: A competency structure connects competencies to learning objectives and activities with achievement criteria.
For an incomplete competency, trace which objective is unmet and inspect its linked activity results and evaluation criteria.
Keep this workflow distinct from the newer Learning Outcomes tool, which this course labels Standards.
Competencies.result: You can explain which required objective or activity is preventing competency achievement.
Competencies.ticket: “The student passed the activity, but the course competency is still incomplete.”
Competencies.scope: Real-screen steps are documented; this destination was not captured and is not interactive in this lab. This competency structure is distinct from the newer Learning Outcomes tool that may be labeled Standards.

Grades.what: Organizes grade items, records scores, calculates totals, and controls which results learners see.
steps: Manage Grades controls structure: categories, maximum points, and weights; Enter Grades holds learner scores.
Settings > Calculation Options controls the math and final-grade type; Org Unit Display Options controls learner-facing display.
For a missing final mark, inspect release status from Enter Grades > Final Calculated Grade > Enter Grades; an entered score is not automatically a released final grade.
Grades.result: Scores and final totals follow the grade book’s calculation and visibility settings.
Grades.ticket: “I entered the marks, but students cannot see their final grade.”
Grades.scope: Many grade-book screens and several saved changes were captured; the lab implements selected workflows and calculations with synthetic data.

Quick Eval.what: Collects supported submissions awaiting evaluation into one work list.
steps: Use the work list to find supported assignment, quiz, and discussion work awaiting evaluation; filter by course or activity to narrow a ticket.
Saving draft feedback leaves evaluation unfinished for learners; publish when feedback is ready to be released.
If expected work is missing, check the original activity and course availability as well as the Quick Eval filters.
Quick Eval.result: Published evaluations leave the pending work list; draft feedback may still require attention.
Quick Eval.ticket: “Where can I see all the work I still need to grade?”
Quick Eval.scope: Real-screen steps are documented; this destination was not captured and is not interactive in this lab.

Quizzes.what: Creates question-based assessments and controls attempts, timing, availability, and result release.
steps: A quiz timer limits attempt duration; availability dates determine the access window, so changing only one may not solve a timing ticket.
For one quiz’s exception, use Special Access; a New Time Limit is an absolute duration, while Classlist accommodations can use a multiplier.
Check the affected learner, access dates, attempts, and timing behavior together before saving the exception.
Quizzes.result: The quiz uses its configured questions and attempt rules, with any applicable learner-specific exceptions.
Quizzes.ticket: “One learner needs more time on this quiz without changing everyone else’s timer.”
Quizzes.scope: Quiz creation, timer, and Special Access controls were captured; real question delivery, learner attempts, and saved exception outcomes were not observed.

Rubrics.what: Defines assessment criteria and achievement levels so evaluation and feedback are consistent.
steps: Analytic rubrics assess several criteria; Holistic rubrics give a single overall judgment, and the scoring choice determines whether and how points are assigned.
Build criteria and level descriptions that explain the report’s expectations, then check rubric status and learner visibility.
Attach the intended rubric to the assessment; a rubric that exists in the tool is not necessarily attached to the activity being graded.
Rubrics.result: The assessment can use the rubric to show expectations and record criterion-based feedback.
Rubrics.ticket: “I want the same marking criteria available when I grade every report.”
Rubrics.scope: Real-screen steps are documented; this destination was not captured and is not interactive in this lab.

Self Assessments.what: Provides ungraded practice questions with immediate feedback for learner reflection.
steps: Use this for formative practice with immediate answer feedback, rather than a scored quiz or an opinion survey.
Create the assessment and its questions, and write feedback that explains mistakes; the feedback is central to its learning value.
Make it available in the course and check the practice experience without expecting a numerical grade-book result.
Self Assessments.result: Learners can check their understanding without creating a numerical grade-book assessment.
Self Assessments.ticket: “Can students practise these questions without the result counting toward their grade?”
Self Assessments.scope: Real-screen steps are documented; this destination was not captured and is not interactive in this lab.

Standards.what: Manages the course’s learning outcomes under the institution’s chosen label, here Standards.
steps: Standards is this institution’s label for Learning Outcomes; other sites may call the same tool Outcomes, Expectations, or Objectives.
Add or import the approved outcomes, then align them to the relevant content, assessment activities, or rubric criteria.
For an achievement question, check both the alignment and the evaluated evidence; merely listing an outcome does not establish learner achievement.
Standards.result: The course can connect learning activities and achievement evidence to its stated expectations.
Standards.ticket: “How do I show which learning standard this assignment assesses?”
Standards.scope: Real-screen steps are documented; this destination was not captured and is not interactive in this lab. Institutions can rename Learning Outcomes, and available outcome workflows depend on configuration.

Surveys.what: Collects learner opinions or feedback without requiring correct answers.
steps: Use Surveys for opinions or feedback; questions do not need correct answers and can include rating scales.
For anonymous mid-course feedback, decide on anonymity before collecting responses, then configure questions, availability, and access.
Review response statistics under the configured anonymity rules rather than expecting quiz-style scores.
Surveys.result: Learners can submit feedback under the configured survey settings.
Surveys.ticket: “I want anonymous feedback about how the course is going.”
Surveys.scope: Real-screen steps are documented; this destination was not captured and is not interactive in this lab.

Announcements.what: Publishes course notices that can appear in the course announcement area.
steps: Headline and Content provide the notice; dates and release conditions determine which learners can see it and when.
For a missing announcement, check whether it was published, its visibility window, and its conditions before posting another copy.
For a room-change message, publish with the intended visibility and verify it in the course; email or push notification delivery also depends on notification settings.
Announcements.result: Eligible learners can read the published notice when its visibility conditions permit it.
Announcements.ticket: “How can I tell the whole class that tomorrow’s room has changed?”
Announcements.scope: Real-screen steps are documented; this destination was not captured and is not interactive in this lab.

Discussions.what: Hosts course conversations in topics organized within forums.
steps: Forums organize topics, while learners post inside topics; restrictions at either level can affect participation.
For a cannot-post ticket, inspect topic availability and posting rules, then check forum visibility and any group or release restrictions.
Confirm the learner belongs to the intended audience and that the topic is open for participation during the required period.
Discussions.result: The intended learners can use the discussion when both its forum and topic settings allow access.
Discussions.ticket: “Students can see the discussion heading but cannot post a reply.”
Discussions.scope: Real-screen steps are documented; this destination was not captured and is not interactive in this lab.

Intelligent Agents.what: Runs rule-based checks that can trigger actions such as messages when learners meet specified criteria.
steps: Agents check criteria when they run; they do not continuously monitor learners, and first-time-only actions differ from actions on every qualifying run.
For an inactivity reminder, configure the matching criteria and recipients, then use Practice Run to inspect who would qualify.
After reviewing matches, enable or schedule the intended action and use View History to investigate unexpected or missing messages.
Intelligent Agents.result: The agent checks criteria when it runs and takes the configured action for matching users.
Intelligent Agents.ticket: “Can the course send a reminder to students who have not logged in recently?”
Intelligent Agents.scope: Real-screen steps are documented; this destination was not captured and is not interactive in this lab.

Course Reset.what: Permanently removes course materials and learner activity data to return a course to an empty shell.
steps: Reset is for deliberately emptying an approved course shell: it removes learning materials and learner activity data while retaining enrollments.
Review the selected course and deletion summary, including optional groups, homepage, navbar, or widget items, and preserve anything required first.
Proceed only when the intended outcome is a permanent reset; it is not a routine way to clear one mistaken grade item.
Course Reset.result: A completed reset removes the selected course data and cannot be undone; course enrollments are retained.
Course Reset.ticket: “This disposable practice course needs to be emptied for another training session.”
Course Reset.scope: Real-screen steps are documented; this destination was not captured and is not interactive in this lab.

Insights Portal.what: Opens the analytics dashboards and reporting tools available under the institution’s license and your permissions.
steps: The portal exposes licensed dashboards within your role’s scope; course-level access does not imply permission to see organization-wide data.
For an engagement comparison, choose the relevant dashboard and inspect its course filters, reporting period, and refresh information.
Use drill-down details where permitted and confirm what the indicator measures before interpreting low engagement as non-participation.
Insights Portal.result: You see analytics within your authorized scope, rather than a live audit of every learner action.
Insights Portal.ticket: “Where can I compare learner engagement across the courses I support?”
Insights Portal.scope: Real-screen steps are documented; this destination was not captured and is not interactive in this lab.

Sharing Groups.what: Defines reusable ePortfolio sharing audiences and permissions.
steps: These define ePortfolio audiences and their permissions, such as who can view or comment on a reflection; they are separate from course project groups.
Check the group’s membership, permissions, and sharing behavior, then use it for the intended ePortfolio artifacts.
For a reviewer who cannot see an item, inspect both the sharing group and the item’s actual sharing settings.
Sharing Groups.result: The selected ePortfolio audience receives the configured access; this does not create assignment teams.
Sharing Groups.ticket: “How can learners share portfolio reflections with the same review group each time?”
Sharing Groups.scope: Real-screen steps are documented; this destination was not captured and is not interactive in this lab.

Tools.what: Controls whether supported tools are enabled for the course.
steps: Tool status controls availability in this course; navbar links and role permissions are separate checks when a tool seems missing.
Locate the tool and inspect its status; enabling or disabling it saves automatically.
After a change, inspect related links and release conditions, because disabling a tool can affect activities that depend on it.
Tools.result: The tool’s course availability changes, while removing a navigation link alone would not disable it.
Tools.ticket: “The tool exists in Brightspace, but it seems to be disabled in this course.”
Tools.scope: Real-screen steps are documented; this destination was not captured and is not interactive in this lab.

Manage Repositories.what: Manages the learning repositories and repository-level settings available to your role.
steps: Repository-level settings govern the shared collection; an individual object’s visibility and the user’s permissions can also affect access.
For missing search results, inspect the intended repository’s access and search settings before republishing the resource.
Change only the relevant repository configuration and verify the result for the intended audience.
Manage Repositories.result: The repository uses the selected settings, while individual learning objects may also have their own access choices.
Manage Repositories.ticket: “Our shared teaching resources are not appearing in repository searches.”
Manage Repositories.scope: Real-screen steps are documented; this destination was not captured and is not interactive in this lab.

Publish.what: Adds supported learning objects to a learning repository for reuse.
steps: Publishing places a supported learning object in a selected repository for reuse; it is not a full course backup.
Choose the object and repository, then supply useful metadata and inspect the visibility and version choices.
Verify that the intended audience can find the published object and that the material does not depend on unsupported course-specific links.
Publish.result: The object becomes available for authorized reuse; this is not a complete backup of all course behavior.
Publish.ticket: “How can I share this learning resource with instructors in other courses?”
Publish.scope: Real-screen steps are documented; this destination was not captured and is not interactive in this lab.

Search.what: Finds learning objects in the repositories you are allowed to search.
steps: Search finds objects in accessible repositories; inspect a result’s contents and suitability before using Retrieve.
Dynamic Link to Newest Version follows updates; Locked Link to This Version fixes the linked version; Copy as Content creates a course copy.
Choose according to the course’s update needs and the object’s supported options; some object types offer import rather than these linking choices.
Search.result: The course receives a link or copy according to your choice; supported reuse options depend on the object type.
Search.ticket: “Can I reuse a colleague’s resource and choose whether future updates appear in my course?”
Search.scope: Real-screen steps are documented; this destination was not captured and is not interactive in this lab.
